title: Gully's first flyer
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Sixteenth annual. Gully asks for the flyer himself this year. Twenty bucks, from his own pocket.

panels.composition: The shack. GULLY, in the uncle's apron — the uncle absent — holding out a twenty. WOOD. BARNABY on a crab pot.

characters.pose: in an apron, holding a twenty

props: last year's two flyers on the wall

balloons.text: Resting. I'm doing it this year.

image.prompt: a boy in a backwards cap wearing a fisherman's apron holding out a twenty-dollar bill in front of a shingle shack, two old crab flyers on the wall, a young man and a small dog

panels.composition: Wood, looking at the twenty, then at Gully in the apron.

balloons.text: I look like me in his apron.

image.prompt: close two-shot of a young man looking at his friend who wears an oversized fisherman's apron

panels.composition: Wood drawing the crab on the spot on the shack's counter. Same crab. Barnaby watching the pen.

image.prompt: a young man drawing a large crab on a flyer on a shack counter while a small dog watches the pen intently

panels.composition: The third flyer on the wall beside the first two. Same crab. The hatching has changed again. Gully pins it with the uncle's thumbtack.

image.prompt: three nearly identical crab flyers in a row on a shingle wall, a boy in an apron pinning the newest one, black and white

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The uncle is 'resting.' Gully takes the derby. The strip notes the apron and nothing else.
